CLIMATE ACTION 
Climate Action Plan (CAP) 
1. Confirmation from SEAI on 100% funding of Lot(ii) of the District Heating Study (9 October 2025).  Lot 
(ii) study will further develop on the potential for Carrick-on-Shannon (Review and identify preferred 
heat source, stakeholder engagement, heat demand profile development, heat demand profile 
development, development of pipework distribution network, highways coordination, techno-
economic modelling. 
2. Eastern & Midlands CARO Border sub regional meeting (10 October 2025), minutes available. 
3. Leitrim Climate Action Week was held 13 – 19 October 2025 in alignment with An Taisce.  In total there 
were 31 no events advertised either online or on location around Co. Leitrim.  There were 15 no events 
organised directly by Leitrim County Council (some in partnership with community groups), 9 no 
events organised directly by Leitrim community groups and 7 organised by An Taisce or adjoining 
local authorities. 
4. Key events - Biodiversity film for Carrick & Mohill secondary schools (Cineplex, 13 October 2025), 
Community Garden Open Day (Mohill, 14 October 2025) WaterLANDS event (Ballinaglera, 15 October 
2025), Household Energy Clinic (Drumshanbo, 16 October 2025), Container Gardening (Organic 
Centre, 17 October 2025) and Seed Saving Workshop (19 October 2025).  3 no staff lunch and learn 
sessions, theme of improving household energy efficiency from Sligo Leitrim Energy Agency (SLEA) (2 
no) and Pio Byrnes in his work with Glinsk SEC. 
5. LGMA & CARO Fleet Management event (15 October 2025). 
6. Meeting of the Decarbonising Zone (DZ) taskforce (16 October 2025), minutes available.  Event in 
Leitrim CA Week with SLEA to encourage home retrofitting in the DZ. 
7. Energy WG meeting (20 October 2025) focus on Energy Elephant and Reduce Your Use Campaign.   
8. Lough Allen College event for TY students on completion of Erasmus+ project which included a study 
on waste management (21 October 2025).  Leitrim CC hosted an event in the Chamber in April this year 
as part of this project. 
9. Subset of the Climate Action Committee visited the Erne Campus Enniskillen (23 October 2025), first 
public building in the UK to achieve Passive Premium and BREEAM ratings. 
10. The LASNTG Climate Action Training Programme webinars continued in Autumn to build capacity in 
the whole of Council CA team with Forestry Programme 2023 – 2027 (18 September 2025), Climate 
Goals in Transport (3 October 2025) & National Bioeconomy Action Plan (17 October 2025 
 
Community Climate Action Programme Fund 
Climate Action continue to work with groups in developing their projects and preparing for drawdown of 
funding in Phase 1.  Project delivery at c. 60% for both strands. 
Phase 2 was formally rolled out for Strand 1 (€300,000 available for community climate action projects) 
on 21 October 2025.  There were 3 public information events in the Library of each electoral area; 13 
October (Ballinamore), 14 October (Manorhamilton), 15 October (Carrick-on-Shannon) during Leitrim CA 
Week.  Presentation to SPC Local Development (6 October 2025) 
 
Biodiversity Action Plan 
The draft Biodiversity Action Plan opened for public consultation on 13 October 2025 (until 10 November 
2025).  The period includes 5 no. public consultation information events across all 3 electoral areas to 
facilitate public information and participation in the process.

LIBRARY SERVICES 
 
 
Almost 9,000 visits were made to the libraries over the course of the month and there were 201 new 
members who joined Leitrim library Service in October. 
During the month of October, the usual events such as book club and writer group meetings as well as 
craft groups, exercise classes, scrabble, bridge and language sessions took place.  There was good usage 
of the Sensory Room at Mohill Library and Cubbie at Manorhamilton Library.

6 
 
Children’s Book Festival 
A wide range of events took place across the Leitrim library branch network during Children’s Book 
Festival, celebrating creativity, storytelling, and community engagement. Each branch contributed to a 
vibrant programme that welcomed children, families, and schools into the library spaces. 
 
• Carrick-on-Shannon Library hosted a festive Halloween-themed Storytime session led by Grainne. 
The event was followed by a creative Bookmark Workshop, where children crafted spooky Halloween 
bookmarks, combining literacy with hands-on artistic expression. 
• Dromahair Library offered open Makerspace sessions throughout the month, facilitated by Stuart 
Lawn. These sessions were attended by both adults and children, providing an opportunity to 
explore creative STEAM technologies in an informal and engaging environment. 
• Manorhamilton Library welcomed storyteller and illustrator Wayne O’Connor for a lively Storytime 
session attended by students from St. Clare’s and Masterson National Schools. Wayne also visited 
Mohill and Drumshanbo Libraries as part of the festival celebrations, bringing his unique storytelling 
style to children across the region. 
• Ballinamore Library hosted two highly successful Children’s Book Festival events, welcoming 
approximately 80 children from two local schools. The young attendees enjoyed energetic and 
engaging Storytime sessions led by Wayne O’Connor and Senior Library Assistant Sarah Garden. 
 
Healthy Leitrim  
The Friends of Breastfeeding Support Group hosted a special Halloween event in collaboration with 
Healthy Ireland, marking the launch of their new fortnightly meet-up in Ballinamore Library.  
As part of the Healthy Ireland initiative, Maj Cunningham delivered an informative talk on Healthy Bones, 
which drew a highly engaged audience. Many attendees are also participants in “Build a Stronger, More 
Mobile You”, a weekly course led by Dillon Keane, making Maj’s talk a perfect complement by providing 
the theory behind the practice. Build a stronger more mobile you Chair Exercises with Dillon Kane 
continue in Drumshanbo and are very well intended. 
 
Ciorcal Comhrá/ Irish Language   
Irish Language session continues to attract strong attendance and enthusiasm in Ballinamore, Mohill 
and Dromahair library. 
 
Local studies 
The Local Studies Librarian hosted an interesting talk by Liam McNiffe about the 1852 Leitrim Election. 
30 people attended and it was a very engaging event between the presenter and the audience. A digital 
version of the talk and PowerPoint presentation will be hosted on www.leitrimdoc.ie

ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, REGENERATION, SUSTAINABLE 
TRANSPORT & EMERGENCY SERVICES 
ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT 
 
Digital Placemaking Strategy 
The strategy “Digital Placemaking: A Strategy for a Connected Leitrim” was launched by Minister Dara 
Calleary for at the Reimagining Rural Ireland (Smart Towns and Villages) National Conference held at 
Lough Rinn Castle on 13th October.  
 
STEM Passport for Inclusion- Maynooth University & ATU 
4 Secondary Schools in Leitrim have been approved to take part in the STEM Passport for Inclusion 
programme Level 6 Award for TY students. Maynooth and ATU have scheduled workshop dates for each 
of the schools and will deliver the workshops in the County; some are taking place in the schools, and 
some sessions are in hubs adjacent to the schools. 
 
Broadband Connection Points – Upgrade of BCP equipment 
The upgrade of the BCP equipment for the 12 BCP sites is almost complete with one to be finalised. 
 
Carrick on Shannon Business Campus 
Building on the completed feasibility study for a proposed Enterprise Hub at Carrick on Shannon 
Business Campus, work advanced on planning for a tender for consultancy services to develop a suite of 
work packages to move the project from concept validation to implementation readiness, through the 
development of a comprehensive business, design and governance framework.  The tender was 
published on the eTenders platform on 31st October and closes on 8th December. 
 
County Promotion 
Work is ongoing in terms of finalising plans, invitees list etc for the Intercounty Promotion Event on Nov 
27th at the Irish Embassy in London.  
Plans are being advanced to host a breakfast meeting with Leitrim Diaspora in London on Nov 28th 
Attended by Minister Dara Calleary, Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht, 
the Smart Towns and Village Conference 2025 ‘Reimagining Rural Ireland’, was held on 13th October 
2025.   
The “Powering Up – Scaling for Impact” event at Carrick Campus, hosted by Norah Casey and involving 
two panel discussions of entrepreneurs and advisors, took place on 3rd October. 
 
Leitrim Diaspora 
Works continues on the development of the framework for the Leitrim Diaspora Strategy, 2026-2030.  
Meetings of both the Diaspora Working Group and Steering Groups are planned for November. 
   
Leitrim Economic Forum and Global Business Network 
There were no meetings of the above groups in October, the next meetings of the groups are on the 5th 
and 10th December, respectively.   
 
DRCD Funded Schemes 
The Department hosted a national conference in Athlone during October with speakers giving 
presentations on all the schemes. The Island Theatre were the only community group to be selected by 
the Department to give a presentation on their project.

8 
 
The RRDF funding announcements were made during October, a total of 30 approvals were made 
throughout the country, of one which was The Arroo Centre, Kinlough, who received funding of €572,334.  
 
 
LOCAL ENTERPRISE OFFICE (LEO) 
Training, Mentoring & Export      
A large number of people received training in October as we ran a series of courses such as a 1:1 Marketing 
Review Clinic, How to Save Your Business Money on Energy Bills; Intellectual Property Office of Ireland 
Information Session; CapCut App Training as well as a Start Your Own Business training course. We also 
commenced a Management Development Training Programme for the Creative Sector called ‘Preparing 
for Retail and Trade Shows’ and this course will conclude in the new year. LEO Leitrim also supported our 
Council colleagues in preparing for the Powering Up – Scaling For Impact event which took place in Carrick 
Business Campus on the 3rd October.  
 
On the 1st of October we ran an in-person training event aimed at Creating Inclusive Workplaces That Help 
Attract and Keep Great People and a separate session looking at How Self-Employed People in the 
Creative Sector Can Work on Their Terms, in Their Way. We were incredible lucky to have secured an 
international speaker, Pete Wharmby, to facilitate these sessions and the feedback from both were very 
positive. 
 
National Women’s Enterprise Day 2025 
Nearly 100 female entrepreneurs, business owners, and managers from across the Northwest gathered at 
Lough Rynn Castle Estate in Mohill on October 16th. The event, hosted by the Local Enterprise Offices of 
Leitrim and Sligo, carried the inspiring theme “Rebel Minds: Women Redefining Enterprise.” The evening 
featured a keynote address by Miriam Simon, an award-winning Business Strategist and Peak 
Performance Mentor with three decades of experience spanning both corporate and entrepreneurial 
sectors. Joining Miriam for a panel discussion were Joanna Frivet, Lawyer and Founder of LegalMoov, an 
Irish legal tech platform and Anna Mannion, Founder of Tri Moon Films Ltd. The event also featured a 
dynamic networking session led by writer and producer Maeve McCormack, who served as M.C. for the 
evening and brought great energy to the discussions. 
All In A Days Work Programmes & Associated Financial Supports 
The “All In A Days Work” campaign continues to be rolled out on the areas of Lean, Green and Digital 
supports.  There is significant growth in demand for all three supports, in particular the Energy Efficiency 
Grant (EEG) and Grow Digital (GD) Voucher.   The EEG, with up to 75% of eligible costs up to a maximum 
grant of €10,000 can be supported following the completion of a Green for Business, Green Start or a SEAI 
Energy Audit.   The GD voucher is a grant covering 50% of eligible costs (minimum grant of €500 up to a 
maximum grant of €5,000) limited to new software subscriptions for a period of 12 and training and 
configuration of the software. 
 
Atlantic Economic Corridor Update:  
Smart Towns & Villages Conference: Re-imaging Rural Ireland- Smart Over 120 people attended the 
conference 2025 at Lough Rynn Castle, Mohill on 13th October. Hosted by Leitrim County Council, the 
event explored how digital innovation and local leadership can transform rural Ireland. Keynotes, expert 
panels, and interactive sessions inspired ideas and stronger community connections.

9 
 
 
Interreg Europe Digital Rural: Leitrim continues its partnership under Interreg Europe. The Digital Rural 
Project empowers rural communities through smart technologies and collaborative policymaking to 
foster sustainable regional development. In October 2025 Leitrim hosted over 50 project partners and 
stakeholders from Estonia, Lativia, Crete, The Netherlands, Poland and Slovenia.  
 
PEACE Plus – DS3 Project 
The DS3 Project under PEACE Plus (Smart Towns & Villages) launches in November 2025, running until 
January 2028. It promotes cross-border collaboration through ICT in community services and economic 
activity. Leitrim County Council leads Work Package 2, with one contract awarded for a mobile fab lab 
and another tender currently live. 
 
Creative Heartlands 
Screen Ireland funding has been secured and a new programme of training and mentoring for the screen 
sector has been developed. The programme launched in October and will run until May 2026. This will 
cover Leitrim, Sligo, and Roscommon.  
 
Northwest Regional Enterprise Plan Implementation 
Northwest Vision Development 
The x3 Chief Executives from Leitrim/Sligo/Donegal are collaborating to develop a Northwest Region 
Vision which will feed into the REP development in 2025. There has been a number of working groups with 
hypotheses presented to the working group. Leitrim CoCo is represented on the project by Director of 
Economic Development and the NW Programme Manager. The outcome will be refined towards Christmas 
with an output event in January. 
 
Energy working group 
A multi-agency supported project is underway which will explore the opportunities available to the region 
with available unused energy from our renewable energy sources in the region e.g. onshore wind energy. 
Opportunities being explored are green energy parks, marketing, hydrogen etc. This package was kicked 
off in October. Leitrim CoCo is represented on the project by Director of Economic Development and the 
NW Programme Manager. 
 
10xNW 2026 
Following a very successful event in 2025, a collaborative course of multiple agencies in the Northwest 
region are coming together to host the 10xNW entrepreneurship exchange in February 2026 in Leitrim. The 
working group have convened and are planning this.  
 
Next REP development 
Currently DETE areundergoing a review of the REP’s with the intention of taking recommendations from 
the review towards the next REP development which is due to kick off Q1 2026.

TOURISM 
Autumn Campaign 
The Autumn Campaign ran successfully throughout September and October, culminating in the 
Halloween break. It achieved excellent engagement across all platforms through a strategic mix of media 
channels, including radio, video-on-demand, digital advertising, and press coverage. The campaign’s 
central call to action directed audiences to www.enjoyleitrim.com. 
 
Influencer Marketing 
In October, travel influencer Chris Connolly, known as ‘ExploreWithCriostoir’, visited Leitrim and 
showcased some of the county’s standout experiences. His itinerary included scenic walking trails, 
Glencar Waterfall, Glenview Museum, and a variety of food and accommodation options. His content will 
help to amplify Leitrim’s appeal to a wider audience. 
 
Irish Stew Podcast Collaboration 
Leitrim County Council hosted John Lee and Martin Nutty, co-founders of the US-based *Irish Stew* 
podcast, which has a global audience across the US, UK, and Australia. During their visit, they conducted 
interviews with local tourism businesses. The resulting podcast series, sponsored by Tourism Ireland US. 
The podcast is currently airing and highlights Leitrim’s unique offerings. 
 
Interreg Europe Presentation 
The Tourism Team presented at the Interreg Europe Digitisation Conference, showcasing the new 
Leitrim Visitor App. Over 45 participants from partner countries across Europe attended. The 
presentation highlighted the app’s benefits for local businesses, visitors, and communities, reinforcing 
Leitrim’s commitment to digital innovation in tourism. 
 
Visitor App Promotion 
A soft launch of the Visit Leitrim App is currently underway. Businesses across the county received 
branded merchandise and training materials to support the rollout. Social media and digital advertising 
campaigns have begun, and user insights will be monitored over the coming weeks to guide further 
refinements. 
 
Festival & Event Grants 
Claims for festival and event grants are actively being processed. Promotional support for upcoming 
events continues, with efforts focused on increasing visibility and driving attendance. 
 
Tourism Officers Network 
Leitrim’s Tourism Officer attended the Tourism Officers Networking event in Monaghan, engaging with 
colleagues from other counties. The meeting focused on festival funding strategies and collaborative 
research, with valuable exchanges on current marketing initiatives. 
 
Social Media Engagement 
Throughout October, the Tourism Team maintained active engagement across Instagram, Facebook, 
and Twitter. The final phase of the county-wide photography competition was hosted, with winning 
entries to be featured in the upcoming Leitrim Calendar. These efforts boosted online interaction and 
strengthened connections with both visitors and the local community.

HOUSING 
Social Housing Applications and Assessments 
To date in 2025, the Housing Department has received a total of 150 new applications for social housing 
support.  Of these, 126 have been assessed – with 97 approved and 29 refused/closed.    2 applications are 
currently undergoing assessment, while 22 have been deemed invalid and require further information. 
There are currently 509 approved applicants on the housing waiting list. 
 
Traveller Accommodation Programme 2025–2029 
The Traveller Accommodation Programme 2025–2029, which commenced on 1st January 2025, sets out 
a target to deliver 20 accommodation units over a five-year period. 
 
As of 31st October 2025, a total of 6 units has been delivered through the Standard Local Authority 
Housing Scheme, representing 30% progress toward the overall target. Three of these units were 
completed during the month of September. 
 
The Housing Department remains focused on progressing delivery in line with the programme’s 
objectives for the remainder of the term.

Social Housing Rent Review 2025 
Rent reviews have taken place for tenants who have returned rent review documents that were issued 
earlier in the year.  New rents will be applied to all social housing tenants from the first week in 
November 2025.   
 
For tenants that did not submit the required documentation or failed to reply, a penalty rent will apply 
to their account from the first week in November.  Housing will then commence the process of assessing 
all RAS and Leasing Tenants rents for application to their accounts in Mid-November 2025.

Acquisitions Programme – October Update 
Progress under the Acquisitions Programme continued steadily throughout October. Although no 
purchases were completed during the month, agreements were reached on four properties with a 
combined estimated value of €770,000. These properties are in various parts of the county, including 
Drumkeeran, Manorhamilton, and Ballinamore. 
 
When added to commitments carried forward from previous years (€976,957), the total value of 
committed acquisitions now stands at €1,746,957. This leaves a remaining budget of €253,043 from the 
€2 million allocation provided by the Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage (DHLGH) 
for 2025.  It is expected that the agreed purchases will be finalised by the end of December 2025. The 
programme continues to prioritise the identification of suitable properties to address housing needs 
across the county.

Forward Planning 
Variation to County Development Plan 2023-2029 
Work has commenced to give consideration to the preparation of a variation to the County Development 
Plan 2023-2029 to increase the quantum of land zoned for residential purposes so as to provide for 50% 
headroom. Ministerial Guidelines instructing Local Authorities to update housing targets in line with the 
revised National Planning Framework issued at the end of July. A report on the development capacity of 
existing zoned residential lands as required pursuant to the Section 28 Guidelines ‘National Planning 
Framework (NPF) Implementation – Housing Growth Requirements’ issued to the Members in late October
